question.problem:
The $3$rd term of a geometric sequence is $1$, and the $8$th term is $243.$ What is the first term of this sequence to exceed
$3\,001?$
question.worked_solution:
Since we are given that ${a}_{3}=1$ and ${a}_{8}=243$, we can find the common ratio $r$ of the sequence, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{n-m} & =\frac{{a}_{n}}{{a}_{m}} \\ {r}^{8-3} & =\frac{{a}_{8}}{{a}_{3}} \\ {r}^{5} & =\frac{243}{1} \\ {r}^{5} & ={3}^{5} \\ r & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since ${a}_{3}=1$ and  $r=3$, we can use the $n$th term formula to solve for ${a}_{1}$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\ {a}_{3} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {3}^{3-1} \\ 1 & ={a}_{1}\cdot {3}^{2} \\ 1 & =9{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =\frac{1}{9}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the $n$th term of the geometric sequence is

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\cdot {3}^{n-1} \\  & ={3}^{-2}\cdot {3}^{n-1} \\  & ={3}^{n-3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We want $n$th term to be greater than $3\,001.$
Hence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{n-3} & >3\,001 \\ \operatorname{log}⁡(3)^{n-3} & >\operatorname{log}⁡(3\,001) \\ (n-3)\operatorname{log}⁡(3) & >\operatorname{log}⁡(3\,001) \\ n-3 & >\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(3\,001)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(3)} \\ n & >\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(3\,001)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(3)}+3\end{aligned}
$$

Estimating the right-hand side using a calculator, we get:

$$
\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(3\,001)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(3)}+3≈10.288
$$

Therefore, the $11$th term is the first term of the sequence that exceeds $3\,001.$
